sources.title: Detecting anomalous citation groups in journal networks
sources.retrieved: Full publisher HTML; relevant Results, Discussion and Methods read
anchors: Results / Overlap with the journal groups suspended from JCR / Figure 2
Methods / Detection of anomalous citation groups / equations 1-3
sources.supports: Journal-level conditional degree/block null; donor OR recipient roles; BH adjustment; selected JCR comparator; imperfect coverage and manual judgment limits.
sources.limitation: Not author-fraud accuracy. Blocks fitted on 2000-2019 aggregate cannot establish prospective earlier-year knowledge-only detection. Additional anomalies not all verified cartels.

sources.title: Toward the Discovery of Citation Cartels in Citation Networks
sources.retrieved: Full publisher HTML; Perspective sections 1-5 read
sources.supports: Conceptual multilayer author/paper representation and artificial RDF/SPARQL demonstration; caution that real-world indictment requires detailed analysis.
sources.limitation: Not empirical population author detection validation. Do not adopt example threshold, probability wording or intent-from-coauthorship assumption. Publisher HTML equations incompletely rendered; not used to reproduce formulas.

sources.title: Random graph models for directed acyclic networks
sources.retrieved: Full arXiv HTML retrieved; sections II, III and V-VI inspected
anchors: II Acyclic graphs and ordered graphs
sources.supports: Degree sequence plus temporal ordering in citation null models; ensemble definition and unequal topology probabilities with multiedges; empirical discrepancies.
sources.limitation: Not a fraud detector; ideal ordered graph does not license deleting uncertain version/date evidence.

sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.retrieved: Full author-hosted scanned PDF; 13 rendered pages inspected (pdftotext has no text layer)
sources.supports: FDR is expected false-discovery fraction; original step-up guarantee has independence assumptions.
sources.limitation: No automatic guarantee for dependent fitted network tests; no author-guilt probability or per-case guarantee.

sources.title: Learning Classifiers from Only Positive and Unlabeled Data
sources.retrieved: Full author-hosted PDF downloaded to task scratch and extracted; sections 2-3 and 7 read
sources.supports: Unlabeled includes positives and negatives; probability rescaling assumes positives selected completely at random.
sources.limitation: Investigation selection cannot be presumed random; no PU estimator implemented or validated here.

sources.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
sources.retrieved: Full publisher HTML; Theoretical Background and relevant Results inspected
anchors: Theoretical Background / ROC combinations of four outcomes
PRC: Precision is an intuitive measure
PRC: baseline moves with class distribution
sources.supports: Precision exposes false-alert burden and depends on class distribution; accuracy/ROC alone can mislead on imbalanced data.
sources.limitation: General metrics/biological experiments, not citation manipulation validation.

sources.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science

anchors: 2.4 Towards a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage

sources.limitation: Pinned preprint, not presented as latest edition; own civil-war reanalysis is not citation-fraud empirical evidence.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks

sources.limitation: Image/text experiments do not validate citation models or an individual's fraud probability; no calibrator implemented.
